title: Diwali Gift Guide 2026: Craft, Textiles and Food Gifts Beyond the Mithai Box
excerpt: This year's Diwali edits from Indian publications point the same way: textile-inspired gift boxes, kansa tableware, craft hampers and chocolate that replaces the standard sweet box.
body:
• Three published Diwali 2026 gift guides — from Grazia India, Homegrown and HELLO! India — converge on craft-led gifts: Indian textiles, handcrafted tableware and small-batch food.
  • For food gifts, the named picks include Bombay Sweet Shop's gourmet hamper, Manam Chocolate's Diwali Celebration Spread and Bon Fiction's box of ten assorted chocolate bars.
  • For the home, Forest Essentials' Tapestries of India boxes draw on Kanjeevaram, Bandhani, Banarasi, Leheriya and Sozni textiles, while Pure Home's first Kansa collection covers dinnerware and pooja thalis.
  • Order early: Diwali falls on November 8, and craft and hamper edits in these guides are seasonal lines that sell through before the festival.

The standard Diwali gift — a ribboned box of mithai bought on the way to dinner — is getting competition. The Diwali 2026 gift guides published by Grazia India and HELLO! India all build their lists around Indian craft: textiles, hand-worked metal and wood, and food made in small batches. The guides differ in price and taste, but the direction is shared — a gift that is still in use after the festival ends.

Food gifts that are not the usual sweet box

Grazia's list leads with the Ultimate Diwali Gourmet Hamper from Bombay Sweet Shop, described as a festive spread that takes the traditional sweet box up a notch and is made for sharing. Homegrown's guide makes the same house a headline pick for mithai with contemporary flavour combinations and playful presentation. For chocolate, Grazia lists Manam Chocolate's Diwali Celebration Spread, a chocolate-led alternative to a mithai assortment, and Bon Fiction's retail pack of ten assorted handcrafted chocolate bars.

Textiles you can gift without guessing a size

HELLO! India's standout craft pick is Forest Essentials' Tapestries of India collection: ten gift boxes pairing body-care products with packaging drawn from Indian textile traditions — Kanjeevaram, Bandhani, Banarasi silk, Leheriya and Kashmiri Sozni embroidery. Its Kalyani box, inspired by Kanjeevaram, carries body care with lime, saffron and oudh; the Kesariya box draws on Rajasthan's Leheriya, and the Noor box on Sozni embroidery. It is a way to gift a textile tradition without buying clothing for someone else.

For the home, and for hosts

For a host gift, HELLO! lists Pure Home's first-ever Kansa collection — dinnerware, pooja thalis, dessert bowls, glasses, chargers and serving pieces in the traditional bell metal. Grazia's craft pick for the table is the Ramya Gift Box from The India Craft Project, which pairs brass Chidiya tea-light holders with playing cards. Homegrown's home section includes Anavila Misra's home collection of textiles and furnishings inspired by the aangan, the inward-facing courtyard of her childhood home in Hashupur, Uttar Pradesh, and a handcrafted heart-shaped cement bowl from Notice for rings, keys and keepsakes.

Self-care, and a gift card that is actually an experience

Both Grazia and the other guides include a self-care route: Grazia lists Kama Ayurveda's Head to Toe Glow Renewal Ritual set, and a Seva Home x Payal Singhal candle and diffuser gift set in jasmine. Homegrown includes a different kind of gift altogether — a Lifeyoga gift card for festive-season wellness, with workshop access bundled for members at different terms.

How to choose

Match the gift to the house you are visiting. Food hampers and chocolate spreads suit large family gatherings where the gift will be opened and shared the same evening. Kansa tableware, textile-inspired boxes and craft pieces suit a close host or a corporate recipient you want to remember the gift in January. With Diwali on November 8, order this week and confirm delivery dates on the brand's own site before paying — seasonal edits in all three guides are limited festive lines, not year-round stock.
